tour.name: Madaba, Mount Nebo, the Baptism Site & the Dead Sea Private Tour from Amman
tour.subtitle: Biblical Jordan and the lowest place on Earth in one private day with a licensed guide and vehicle: the 6th-century mosaic map of Madaba, the view from Mount Nebo where Moses looked over the Promised Land, the baptism site of Jesus on the Jordan, and an afternoon floating in the Dead Sea.

tour.overview:
South-west of Amman, the road descends from the plateau to the Dead Sea, the lowest point on land at about 430 metres below sea level, so salty that you float effortlessly. On the way lie the places of the Bible: Madaba, the 'city of mosaics', whose Byzantine map shows Jerusalem and the Holy Land; Mount Nebo, from which, according to the Bible, Moses saw the Promised Land; and Bethany Beyond the Jordan, the site of the baptism of Jesus, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

This private day takes you there with a licensed guide and a vehicle, ending with time on a Dead Sea beach.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Amman
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, vehicle and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• Madaba and its mosaic map.
• Mount Nebo.
• The baptism site.
• The Dead Sea.

WHY THIS WORKS
A private vehicle links these sites at your pace and leaves time to relax at the Dead Sea.

WHO IT SUITS
Families, pilgrims, couples and anyone wanting to float in the Dead Sea.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For Roman Jordan, choose our Jerash and Amman tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Do not shave on the day before; the salty water stings small cuts. Keep the water away from your eyes.

days.name: Madaba, Mount Nebo, the baptism site and the Dead Sea
days.description:
What to expect: biblical Jordan and the Dead Sea, with a licensed guide, private vehicle, entrances and a resort day pass with lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 8:30 and drive to Madaba. In the Greek Orthodox Church of St George, you see the mosaic map laid in the 6th century, showing the Holy Land from Lebanon to Egypt, with a detailed plan of Jerusalem and its Church of the Holy Sepulchre.

On Mount Nebo, you see the Memorial Church of Moses, with its Byzantine mosaics of hunting scenes and animals, and the serpentine cross sculpture; on clear days the view reaches the Dead Sea, Jericho and Jerusalem. You descend to Bethany Beyond the Jordan, where a guide leads you through the tamarisk thickets to the remains of Byzantine churches and the river, the traditional site of the baptism of Jesus by John the Baptist.

In the afternoon, you relax at a Dead Sea resort, with lunch and time to float in the dense salty water, cover yourself with mineral-rich black mud and swim in the pools, before driving back to Amman.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Pick-up in Amman.
09:15 – Madaba.
10:30 – Mount Nebo.
11:45 – Baptism site.
13:30 – Lunch at a Dead Sea resort.
14:30 – Float in the Dead Sea.
17:00 – Drive back.
18:00 – Back in Amman.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Bring swimwear and a towel; resorts provide showers.
• A sunset at the Dead Sea can be arranged.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, licensed guide, entrances, resort day pass with lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: spa treatments, drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Can everyone float in the Dead Sea?
faq.answer: Yes, the salt makes floating effortless; do not swim on your front or put your head under.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, at a Dead Sea resort.

faq.question: Is the resort private?
faq.answer: You use the shared beach and pools of a resort with a day pass.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, for children who can keep the water out of their eyes.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. Resorts have accessible paths; the baptism site trail is flat.

faq.question: Can we stay at the Dead Sea?
faq.answer: Yes, a night at a resort can be added.

faq.question: Is the mud good for the skin?
faq.answer: It is rich in minerals and many find it beneficial; do a small test if your skin is sensitive.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Modest clothes for the religious sites, swimwear and sandals for the beach.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: October to May. Summer at the Dead Sea is very hot.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary in Jordan: guides and drivers appreciate a tip if you were happy with their service, but it is always your choice.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
